method: Dependency DAG built from the seventeen activation cards in planning/components.json (the concept's sixteen plus P17, which D75 and ADR-0003 add): subsystem edges from the subsystem graph (export-062), external producers (Imago, Nucleus, Golusoris, upstream), toolchain admissions and hardware needs. Milestones are bounded, verifiable states. Each is costed (trivial=1, small=2, medium=4, large=8), scored by the number of milestones it transitively unblocks, and flagged for hardware or unverified cross-repository contracts. Ranking takes the available milestone (all blockers ranked) with the highest (1 + transitive unblocks) / cost, under hard rules: (1) done or purely local work ranks before anything needing hardware or an unverified cross-repository contract; (2) the first cross-repository milestone is stack.md step 2 (M09: pin Imago/Nucleus schemas and test one request/result pair locally), preceded by the Aegis-owned schema authoring (M18); (3) exactly one first component (P06, M02) is promoted end-to-end before any second component; (4) build, boot and release milestones are blocked with the evidence that unblocks them; (5) state=ready iff every blocked_by milestone is done. Ties break toward the milestone with more transitive unblocks, then toward the critical path to the first artifact (M11), then toward milestones without an unverified external contract in their own flags or ancestry, then toward milestones without hardware. blocked_by lists direct blockers only; unblocks is its exact inverse.

epics.acceptance: Positive: if admitted, `mkosi summary` parses the Output stanza. Negative: a version below the floor is refused. Boundary: the floor version itself is accepted.

evidence: Disclosure, because a milestone that edits its own bar must say so where the bar is judged: three of this milestone's eleven exit criteria were rewritten in planning/roadmap.json during this delivery and before the state moved to done. None is a relaxation. Criterion 4 read 'Toolchain admission: if D14 keeps mkosi validation in Aegis, mkosi is selected through the template matrix at or above the v24 floor before `mkosi summary` runs; otherwise mkosi validation is deferred to the Imago result'; an either/or cannot be judged done, so it now records the branch that was actually taken and the exact pin `mkosi 27` that supersedes the inherited 'mkosi v24+' floor. Criterion 9 read 'D56 is recorded: mkosi is not installed and M18 takes D14's "validate through the Imago result" branch, or mkosi is pinned at extra/mkosi 27-1 which supersedes the register's inherited "mkosi v24+" row with an exact pin'; its first half is false on the reference profile -- mkosi 27 is installed -- and the Imago-result branch has no result to defer to while Imago is a scaffold, so the criterion now names the Aegis-side branch and why the other is unavailable. Criterion 11 read 'The kernel requirement schema expresses the realtime and scheduler options P07 and P08 need (preemption model, timer frequency, sched_ext, BPF LSM, BTF), because Nucleus builds the kernel and a distribution package is only an interim fixture source (D70)'; it is strictly strengthened by adding the Kconfig-fragment requirement that D70 as amended (PR #93) makes M26's input. No other criterion changed: 1-3, 5-8 and 10 are judged exactly as they were written.

crates/aegis-fabrica-defs carries both M18 schemas: src/manifest.rs (ProductInputManifest: correlation id, exact 40-character revision, pinned distribution snapshot, repart/sysupdate/mkosi/kernel-requirement references, package set, boot kernel identity, bounded retries) and src/kernel.rs (KernelRequirement: feature rows, ABI bounds, accepted architectures, artifact digest and signature), both built on the ten bounded field types in src/field.rs that validate during decoding through #[serde(try_from = "String")]; `cargo build --locked` exits 0

The reviewed manifest build/product-input.json validates the M03 files: crates/aegis-fabrica-defs/tests/product_input_manifest.rs reads the five drop-ins in build/repart.d and the transfer in build/sysupdate.d and runs them through the same RepartDefinition and TransferDefinition parsers the M03 gate uses. A set that does not parse is DefinitionRefused, a set that parses but drops the alternate root slot is RequirementNotMet with MissingAlternateRootSlot{slots:1}, and a manifest without a correlation id, without a 40-character revision, or with snapshot "latest" does not decode at all. Verified by `cargo test --locked --all-features`

The kernel requirement is a payload rather than a fixed symbol list: build/kernel-requirement.json carries thirteen {symbol, state, probe, required-by} rows and the crate names no Kconfig symbol in code. `grep -rn 'CONFIG_[A-Z]' crates/aegis-fabrica-defs/src` returns four hits, all inside documentation comments (three `CONFIG_X` placeholders and one `CONFIG_BPF_LSM` example)

D07 (boot kernel identity) and D18 (distribution release and package pinning) are recorded in docs/roadmap/README.md and are carried by the schema rather than only by prose: the manifest's kernel block can spell all three D07 sources (distribution-package, built-here, producer-artifact) and records the pinned default package linux-rt alongside the source in force, and D18's pin is the SnapshotId field type, which refuses "latest" and "rolling" during decoding

mkosi is admitted with an exact pin read back from the reference profile: `mkosi --version` prints `mkosi 27` and `pacman -Qi mkosi` reports Version 27-1 installed from repository extra. docs/roadmap/toolchain-admission.md replaces M03's 'installed and not admitted' paragraph with the row, superseding the M01 register's inherited 'mkosi v24+' floor with the exact pin

`mkosi summary` parses the Output stanza of the reviewed build/mkosi.conf: `python3 tools/verify_mkosi_definitions.py` exits 0 with mkosi/positive exit 0 (Output Format disk, Output aegis-os.raw, Image ID aegis-os, Snapshot 2026/09/13, and Repart Directories resolving to the reviewed build/repart.d), mkosi/negative-below-floor exit 1 with `mkosi 28 or newer is required by this configuration (found 27)`, and mkosi/boundary-at-floor exit 0 at MinimumVersion=27. The gate is wired into `make verify-all` as `make verify-mkosi` and skips with a reason on a host without mkosi or below the floor. The gate also asserts the absence of an unreviewed partition-definition set rather than only the presence of the reviewed one: exactly one resolved `RepartDirectories=` row must be the reviewed directory, compared as a resolved path rather than by the tail of the path, and any other row holding a `.conf` fails the case by name. Reproduced before and after: a `build/mkosi.conf.d/99-stowaway.conf` drop-in adding a second `RepartDirectories=` row that points at another directory ending `build/repart.d` was accepted with exit 0 by the suffix test, and is refused with exit 1 by the resolved-path test, while the reviewed definition with no drop-in still exits 0. This matters because git cannot track an empty directory, so a `mkosi.repart/` or `mkosi.conf.d/` tree can exist in a checkout, be read by mkosi as a default path, and never appear in `git status` or any diff

Each asserted feature is traceable to its probe command, and the probe's path is asserted against the same capability's evidence command in planning/hardware-profile.json. Read back on the reference profile: `zgrep CONFIG_PREEMPT_RT /proc/config.gz` prints `# CONFIG_PREEMPT_RT is not set`; `zgrep CONFIG_PREEMPT_DYNAMIC /proc/config.gz` prints `CONFIG_PREEMPT_DYNAMIC=y`; `zgrep CONFIG_HZ_1000 /proc/config.gz` prints `CONFIG_HZ_1000=y`; `cat /sys/kernel/security/lsm` prints `capability,landlock,lockdown,yama,bpf`; `ls /sys/kernel/btf/vmlinux` lists the blob; `ls /sys/class/powercap` lists intel-rapl, intel-rapl:0 and intel-rapl:0:0; `ls /sys/kernel/iommu_groups | wc -l` prints 38

Positive against a real reference payload: build/kernel-requirement.reference.json is satisfied by planning/hardware-profile.json with no unmet row -- architecture x86-64, kernel release 7.2.4-1-cachyos, the module ABI, thirteen Kconfig symbol states and the four runtime capabilities the probes read

Negative bound to a measured absence: build/kernel-requirement.json, the product requirement, is refused against the same profile with exactly one unmet row, StateMismatch for CONFIG_PREEMPT_RT (required built-in, observed not set). The reference kernel is PREEMPT_DYNAMIC, so this workstation is not a kernel the product requirement admits

Boundary: a payload demanding only CONFIG_HZ_1000 is accepted against the same profile that refuses the product requirement, and relaxing only the CONFIG_PREEMPT_RT row makes the product requirement pass with no other change. The schema therefore discriminates per feature and not per kernel flavour

The payload is expressible as the kernel configuration fragment M26 consumes: KernelRequirement::config_fragment renders CONFIG_PREEMPT_RT=y, CONFIG_HZ_1000=y, CONFIG_SCHED_CLASS_EXT=y, CONFIG_BPF_LSM=y, CONFIG_DEBUG_INFO_BTF=y and CONFIG_VFIO=m -- one assignment per feature row with its requirement identifier on the line above, and no line that is neither a comment nor an assignment. The renderer validates before it writes a line and returns the refusal otherwise, because every field of the payload is public: a caller that assembled a requirement without decoding it would otherwise receive a fragment silently short of the rows past the feature bound, and M26 applies this fragment to a base configuration. A payload at MAX_FEATURES renders 64 assignments; one row past it is refused with TooMany{what: "features"} instead of rendering 64

No producer repository is contacted and no gate here needs a network: `unshare -rn cargo test --locked --all-features --offline` exits 0 over 29 test binaries and two doc-test groups, 275 cases with no failure, and `unshare -rn mkosi --no-pager --directory build summary` exits 0

Gates re-run on the reference profile, each exit 0: `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo build --locked`, `cargo test --locked --all-features` (275 cases over 29 test binaries and two doc-test groups), `cargo clippy --locked --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`, `RUSTDOCFLAGS='-D warnings' cargo doc --locked --no-deps`, `python3 tools/verify_preparation.py`, `python3 tools/rank_roadmap.py`, `python3 -B -m unittest discover -s tools -p 'test_*.py'` (113 tests), `make verify-all`, `make verify-mkosi`, `npx markdownlint-cli2`, `yamllint .`, `flake8 .` and `black --check --line-length 100`

Scope: development evidence on the reference profile recorded in planning/hardware-profile.json. What was produced is two schemas, three reviewed payload files, one reviewed image definition and a configuration parse. No image, UKI, kernel, artefact, signature or boot evidence is produced or claimed, no producer repository is contacted, and the image, kernel, boot, hardware and release gates remain blocked

Dated 2026-09-29, appended after done (D103, D104, D105 and a defect found by probe); no exit criterion or epic text changes, and criterion 2's 'accepted architectures' now reads all-of. The array form: KernelRequirement::decode, and ProductInputManifest::decode likewise, accepted a payload written as a JSON array of its values in declaration order, because serde's derived decoder implements visit_seq and deny_unknown_fields has no key to refuse there -- a malformed payload criterion 1 and E18-2 should have refused. Every struct of both contracts now decodes from a JSON object only, at the top and nested (src/payload.rs); tests/array_form.rs sends the array form of both payloads and of every nested struct, and a one-element array led by another version, which the object-only version peek alone decides, and its negative cases fail against the decoder of 061bbde. D103: required-by admits exactly the identifiers of the form nucleus's ADR-0007 states, an upper-case letter then [A-Z0-9-], at most 128 bytes, with the bare REQ- refused; the REQ- form binds the payloads Aegis issues (RequirementId::is_aegis_requirement, tests/issued_payloads.rs). D104: a listed architecture is a promise, so a profile reports each other listed architecture as ArchitectureUnverified and MAX_UNMET grows by MAX_ARCHITECTURES, which tests/reference_profile.rs holds by building the reachable maximum, four rows plus two for each of MAX_FEATURES features; both reviewed payloads list x86-64 alone, so exit criteria 6 to 8 hold unchanged. D105: build/kernel-requirement.schema.json and build/product-input.schema.json are generated from the types with schemars 1.2.2 and held to them by tests/json_schema.rs; tools/test_payload_schemas.py validates the three reviewed payloads against them. `cargo test --locked --all-features` passes on the pinned toolchain, and criterion 5 still holds for the crate: it contacts no producer.

reference_profile.rationale: Unmoved at rank 5 but materially cheaper and materially better evidenced. The schema can now be authored against a measured reference payload instead of an invented one, and — this is the part the profile uniquely enables — the NEGATIVE case is genuinely falsifiable here: a manifest requiring CONFIG_PREEMPT_RT must be rejected against this host, because `zgrep` returns '# CONFIG_PREEMPT_RT is not set' for the running kernel, and the profile records the same absence as its realtime_kernel capability.

milestones.title: P02 A/B candidate lifecycle state machine
exit_criteria: The A/B lifecycle (candidate, signature check, delta acquisition, slot swap, watchdog, bless or rollback) is a Rust library with manifest, lock (location per D15) and positive, negative and boundary tests
D13 (reversible consolidation versus permanent hardening) is recorded against the dm-verity requirement
Uses the Rust toolchain admitted in M02; systemd and sysupdate calls are stubbed
The state machine exposes a machine-readable transition trace so that M24 can diff a real QEMU A/B sysupdate transfer against it byte-for-byte rather than by narrative comparison.
milestones.cheapest_exit: Model the lifecycle as a pure state machine with a stubbed clock and stubbed sysupdate.

epics.title: A/B lifecycle state machine
epics.acceptance: Positive: the happy path reaches Bless. Negative: a signature failure reaches Discard. Boundary: watchdog expiry exactly at the timeout takes Rollback, and one tick before does not.

epics.title: Reversible consolidation decision
epics.acceptance: The decision is recorded, and a test shows that a reopened slot still requires a verity match before Bless.

evidence: crates/aegis-janus-lifecycle (D15) is a workspace member with its manifest and the committed Cargo.lock: the P02 A/B candidate lifecycle as a pure state machine over candidate, signature check, delta acquisition, slot swap, watchdog and bless or rollback, plus the D13 reopening. 84 integration tests and 1 doc test pass under `cargo test --locked --all-features -p aegis-janus-lifecycle`, and tests/public_surface.rs fails on any public item no integration test names, sweeping 186 public names. The sweep reads public struct fields and pub static as declarations, not only keyword-introduced items: TraceHeader, TraceLine, DecisionRecord and Citation are all-public-field structs and their 13 field names were outside the sweep until the M15 verification planted an untested pub field and an untested pub static and watched both pass. MINIMUM_SURFACE is set at 180, above the 173 names the keyword arms collect alone, so dropping the field arm again fails the bound

The watchdog boundary REQ-P02-08 asks about is the half-open interval [armed_at, due_at), so expiry is now >= due_at, and the expiry is a property of the deadline rather than of the event that samples it: an on-trial state reads the clock and evaluates the deadline before it dispatches the event, so past due_at every offered event plans RolledBack + Disarm, a Bless included, and the D13 maintenance window is bounded the same way. tests/watchdog_boundary.rs forks one machine and drives copies at due-1, due and due+1 three times over -- Tick on the armed watchdog, Bless on the armed watchdog with no Tick ever offered, and Bless on a reopened maintenance window, again with no Tick -- so each triple differs in the clock reading and in nothing else, and two negative tests show that a late Remeasure and an event the window would otherwise refuse both roll back. The forced rollback is traced under the event that was offered, not under a Tick nobody sent. Before this was fixed the deadline was consulted only for Event::Tick, so a driver that never offered one blessed a candidate whose watchdog had expired: observed at armed_at=1000, due_at=1600, Bless at tick 1000000 returning Ok(Blessed) on the same machine value on which Tick returned RolledBack. The clock is a parameter and never ambient -- Machine::step takes a Clock, StubClock is the only implementation the crate ships, and a clock that steps backwards is refused by a monotonic guard instead of accepted; verified by cargo test --locked --all-features

D13 is recorded and reconciled with the dm-verity requirement: decision::D13_CONSOLIDATION is Closed on reversible structural consolidation with permanent hardening still representable, reconciling REQ-P02-05, REQ-P02-01 and REQ-P16-05 against dispute DSP-27 and citing export-004 15831276a058 and export-011 528da609dab7 by export id and digest prefix only. The register is descriptive and the machine holds the rule: reopening a blessed slot discards the held dm-verity measurement, so a re-bless is refused with VerityUnmeasured until a fresh measurement is reported, and with VerityMismatch when that measurement differs from the signed release by a single nibble; verified by tests/consolidation_decision.rs

The transition trace is designed as the artefact M24 consumes rather than as a log: JSON Lines, one header line naming the release, both slots and the signed root hash, then one record per accepted step with a dense ascending sequence number, every line carrying the schema tag aegis.p02.ab-transition.v1 and a record kind, and no floating point, map ordering, host timestamp or free text anywhere in it. Rendering is a fixed point of Trace::parse, which is what makes expected.render() == observed_text sound in either direction; tests/transition_trace.rs holds the happy path against a golden seven-line rendering byte for byte and refuses a foreign schema tag, a misplaced record kind, a broken sequence, a slot pair that is not an A/B pair, an unknown field, a header whose count was tampered downward, and a body cut short -- the last being the direction a trace is actually lost in: dropping the golden trace's last body line is refused as TraceError::Count { declared: 6, found: 5 } rather than read as the shorter history it looks like. The M15 verification found that only the tampered-header direction had been covered; verified by cargo test --locked --all-features

systemd and sysupdate calls are stubbed structurally rather than by promise: the crate depends only on base16ct, serde, serde_json and thiserror at the versions Cargo.lock already pinned, declares no binary and no build script, and tests/stubbed_effects.rs sweeps all eleven src files with comments stripped for twenty recorded identifiers -- std::process, Command, std::fs, File, OpenOptions, SystemTime, Instant, std::net, std::env, std::io, std::os, std::path, std::thread, env!, option_env!, include!, include_str!, include_bytes!, unsafe and libc -- and finds none. The list is an enumeration and not a quantifier, and the evidence says so: it is not every identifier through which the host could be reached, because no list of identifiers is that. The M15 verification showed it by planting option_env!, std::path::Path::new(..).exists(), std::os::unix::net::UnixStream::connect(..), std::io::Write::flush and std::thread::current() past the earlier fourteen-token list and watching the sweep pass and clippy exit 0; the six tokens that close those five reaches are now on the list, the planted function is kept in the test file as the input the widened list has to catch (re-run against the verifier's plant crate, it now reports all five), and the claim in docs/build/ab-lifecycle.md, CHANGELOG.md and crates/README.md is restated as a regression gate over an enumeration resting on a structural argument -- no unsafe anywhere, no libc, no binary, no build script, four pinned dependencies -- rather than as a proof of purity. SysupdateCall describes the six calls a real implementation would make and StubSysupdate answers them from a script; nothing runs systemd-sysupdate, opens a device, computes a hash, changes a boot order or reboots. Open point, not settled here: sysupdate.d(5) defines a Verify= key that build/sysupdate.d/10-root.transfer does not set, so the signature stage is modelled and is not claimed of the reviewed definition

HISS-03 is recorded as a falsifiable claim rather than an absolute one: a transition allocates nothing because every value the machine holds is Copy and the trace is a fixed [Transition; 32] array, and tests/allocation_bounds.rs binds that to Machine: Copy and to a recorded size bound, so adding a Vec, String or Box anywhere inside the machine stops the test compiling and fails the gate. Measured under a counting global allocator: 0 allocations for Machine::new, for every step kind of the happy path, for the whole happy path taken together, for a refused step, for pending_call, for StubSysupdate::invoke, and for each of the five forced-rollback steps the expired deadline now plans. Rendering and parsing a trace do allocate, they are not the lifecycle path, and the crate documentation says so instead of claiming the crate allocates nowhere

Gates on the pinned Rust 1.98.1 toolchain from rust-toolchain.toml, with no new toolchain and no new third-party dependency: cargo fmt --check, cargo build --locked, cargo test --locked --all-features (295 tests across the workspace, up from 210 before this milestone), cargo clippy --locked --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings and RUSTDOCFLAGS=-D warnings cargo doc --locked --no-deps all exit 0; make verify-all exits 0, carrying the Python preparation tests, tools/verify_preparation.py, make verify-systemd, praetorctl compile-context --verify, praetorctl audit and the workspace crate gate. git status --porcelain Cargo.lock reports the workspace member and nothing else

The milestone was put through an adversarial verification that reproduced each finding in a throwaway probe crate before it was closed and re-ran the probe after. It found one behavioural defect against REQ-P02-08, the first requirement of epic E15-1 -- the watchdog deadline was evaluated only for Event::Tick, so a candidate whose watchdog had expired was still blessed when the driver never offered one, and a reopened slot whose bounded window had closed still accepted Remeasure and Bless -- and three overstated or uncovered claims: a universal claim over what was a fourteen-token deny list, a public-surface sweep blind to public struct fields and pub static, and an evidence sentence claiming coverage of a truncated trace that no test produced. All four are closed above, each with the triples that hold the fix, and the wording of the two overstatements is corrected in the tracked files rather than only widened in the code. The verification is development evidence about the model on one workstation and closes no image, boot, hardware or release gate

Scope limit: a pure state machine with stubbed effects, run on one workstation. No image is built, nothing boots, and no real A/B swap, slot write, signature check, dm-verity computation or reboot happens; no TPM is touched and no device is opened. P02 aegis-janus-vallum stays a proposal in planning/components.json because this crate models the lifecycle and is not the component daemon, and P02's activation blockers are image, kernel, boot and hardware evidence this milestone produces none of. M24 becomes ready; M11, M20 and the image, boot and release gates remain blocked and this milestone claims none of their evidence

reference_profile.rationale: Rank unchanged at 6, but its unblocks target changes from M11 to the new M24 boot-evidence harness. That is a real improvement: the A/B state machine is now compared against a REAL observed transition on the reference profile at M24 (rank 14) instead of waiting for an Imago artifact at old rank 16. M15's transitive unblock count rises from 4 to 5 and its score from (1+4)/2 to (1+5)/2 = 3.0, which is still short of M18's 4.5 in the same tier, so the gain lands as better evidence rather than as a new position: M15 stays at rank 6, behind M18.

milestones.title: Trivial leaf slices: P03 Vulcan and P15 Hestia validation crates
exit_criteria: aegis-vulcan and aegis-hestia are added as workspace members (they are absent from the proposal workspace) with manifests, lock entries and positive/negative/boundary tests; the Rust toolchain from M02 is reused
Scaffold assertions are refactored to Result per HISS-07 so that negative cases are ordinary tests
The Hestia location decision (D09) is applied from the M01 inventory

Interface contracts are typed for P03 to P09 (weight streaming descriptor), P03 to P15 (media ingest descriptor) and P15 to P04 (overlay registration), each with a negative test for a malformed payload; the transports stay stubbed until M12

The P03-to-P09 weight-streaming descriptor and the P03-to-P15 media-ingest descriptor are typed so that the reference profile's actual DMA-BUF export path (i915 renderD129, amdgpu renderD130, nvidia_drm modeset=Y) can be bound at M25 without reshaping the descriptor.

epics.title: Vulcan validation crate
epics.acceptance: Positive: an aligned BAR is accepted. Negative: a misaligned BAR is rejected. Boundary: block_count 0 and 8193 are rejected, 8192 is accepted, and the ring index wraps.

epics.title: Hestia vector-store state machine
epics.acceptance: Positive: an initialized store answers queries. Negative: a query before init fails. Boundary: limits 0 and 101 fail, and 1 and 100 pass.

epics.title: P03 and P15 interface contracts
epics.acceptance: Positive: the descriptors round-trip. Negative: a malformed descriptor is rejected. Boundary: a descriptor at the maximum block count is accepted, and one over is rejected.

evidence: crates/aegis-vulcan and crates/aegis-hestia are workspace members. The root Cargo.toml lists five members written out one per line with no glob, Cargo.lock gains a [[package]] entry for each (serde, serde_json and thiserror only; no new third-party crate is resolved), and `git status --porcelain Cargo.lock` shows the lock modified rather than regenerated. The Rust toolchain admitted at M02 is reused unchanged: `rustup show active-toolchain` prints 1.98.1-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu overridden by rust-toolchain.toml, and neither rust-toolchain.toml nor docs/roadmap/toolchain-admission.md is edited. Both crates are libraries: no [[bin]], publish = false, and [lints] workspace = true so unsafe_code = "forbid" is inherited rather than restated

The scaffold assertions are refusals, not panics (HISS-07). The three P03 assertions become VulcanError::BarMisaligned (BarAddress::new), VulcanError::BarUnmapped (UserSpacePcieDriver::execute_direct_dma) and VulcanError::BlockCountOutOfRange (BlockCount::new); the three P15 assertions become HestiaError::NotInitialised (PgliteVectorStore::query), HestiaError::QueryLimitOutOfRange (QueryLimit::new) and HestiaError::InvalidDmaBufFd (DmaBufFd::new). crates/aegis-vulcan/tests/scaffold_assertions.rs and crates/aegis-hestia/tests/scaffold_assertions.rs enumerate the three each, show every negative case as an ordinary test, and sweep their own src/ for seven aborting constructs -- assert!, assert_eq!, assert_ne!, panic!, unreachable!, .unwrap() and .expect() -- finding none outside comments. Each of the seven is itself checked to be one the sweep reports, against planted text, because a watched list is a gate only where its entries are reachable: the M17 verification planted a reachable unreachable! in library code and the list, the workspace clippy set and the whole suite all passed over it. The workspace now denies clippy::unreachable and clippy::exit as well, so every crate is covered and not only the two carrying this sweep

E17-1 is satisfied in crates/aegis-vulcan. Positive: BarAddress::new(0xf7200000) is accepted and UserSpacePcieDriver::map_bar returns the 16384-byte window (tests/bar_alignment.rs). Negative: 0xf7200001 is refused as BarMisaligned and is not rounded to the nearest page. Boundary: BlockCount::new refuses 0 and 8193 and accepts 8192, whose transfer_bytes is exactly 4 MiB (tests/block_bounds.rs); and RingIndex::LAST.advance() is RingIndex::ZERO at NVME_RING_SIZE 1024, while RingIndex::ZERO.advance() is 1 (tests/ring_index.rs)

E17-2 is satisfied in crates/aegis-hestia/tests/vector_store.rs. Positive: an initialised store answers a query of limit 5 with 5 hits and reports the recorded 256 MB buffer. Negative: the same query on an uninitialised store is NotInitialised and leaves the store uninitialised. Boundary: QueryLimit::new refuses 0 and 101 and accepts 1 and 100, and an initialised store answers at both ends of that range

E17-3 is satisfied across both crates. Positive: WeightStreamDescriptor and MediaIngestDescriptor round-trip through encode_into/decode (crates/aegis-vulcan/tests/contract_weight_stream.rs, contract_media_ingest.rs), and so does OverlayRegistration (crates/aegis-hestia/tests/contract_overlay_registration.rs). Negative: each has a malformed-payload case -- empty text, an empty object, an added unknown field under deny_unknown_fields, and a renamed version tag that decodes as UnknownVersion rather than leniently; the media-ingest schema additionally refuses a misaligned BAR address, and the overlay schema refuses a negative DMA-BUF descriptor and a non-overlay layer. Boundary: a descriptor carrying "blocks":8192 decodes and one carrying 8193 or 0 does not, for both P03 schemas

The DMA-BUF export path is a field of both P03 descriptors, so M25 binds values rather than reshaping a schema. DmaBufExport carries a RenderNode (the DRM minor, 128..=191, rendered as renderD<minor>), a DrmDriver and a ModesetState. The reference profile was probed on this workstation on 2026-09-13: `ls /dev/dri` lists renderD128, renderD129 and renderD130; `readlink -f /sys/class/drm/renderD<n>/device/driver` resolves to nvidia, i915 and amdgpu respectively; `cat /sys/module/nvidia_drm/parameters/modeset` prints Y; `cat /sys/module/amdgpu/parameters/modeset` prints -1; and /sys/module/i915/parameters/modeset is root-readable only, so an unprivileged probe cannot distinguish it from the driver default. Those three readings are REFERENCE_PROFILE_EXPORTS, and crates/aegis-vulcan/tests/dmabuf_export.rs binds each of them into both descriptors and requires all six payloads to round-trip. The tri-state modeset field exists because two of the three readings are a driver default rather than an explicit yes

Decision D09 is applied. The register crates/aegis-hestia/src/decision.rs records the closed decision -- both a Rust crate and a Svelte package, joined by a typed boundary -- with its two sources cited by export id and digest prefix, and keeps the two rejected options representable. The boundary itself is crates/aegis-hestia/src/view.rs: HestiaView is a versioned, bounded, Copy snapshot the crate renders and the package would read. It carries no method, handle or DMA-BUF descriptor, which tests/d09_boundary.rs asserts by serialising a snapshot of a registered surface and requiring the descriptor number to be absent. No Svelte package, manifest, lockfile or accessibility test is added by this milestone and none is claimed; D10 has still to pin the toolchain that would build one

The transports stay stubbed. Neither crate opens a device, maps a window, issues a transfer, starts a store or connects to a compositor. crates/aegis-vulcan/tests/stubbed_effects.rs sweeps the crate's own src/ for 22 named identifiers (memmap2, mmap, MmapOptions, libc, /dev/vfio, /dev/dri, ioctl, cuda, RawFd and the rest) and crates/aegis-hestia/tests/stubbed_effects.rs for 20 (std::fs, postgres, sqlx, wayland, smithay, Command, RawFd and the rest); both fail if one appears outside a comment. These are regression gates over those two named enumerations, not proofs that no effect of any kind is reachable: an identifier that is not on a list is not checked. What narrows the remaining surface is the dependency set, which tests/manifest_hygiene.rs pins to serde, serde_json and thiserror in each crate

HISS-03 is stated as a falsifiable property rather than as an absolute. Every value on a decision path in both crates is Copy, which tests/allocation_bounds.rs enforces by requiring Copy of 17 types in aegis-vulcan and 16 in aegis-hestia -- a Vec, String or Box at any depth stops the file compiling. Decoding is explicitly not claimed to be allocation-free: both files decode a payload whose correlation identifier is spelled with a \u006d JSON escape, which serde_json unescapes into a heap scratch buffer, and assert only that it decodes to the same value. The PgliteVectorStore is Copy only because StoragePath is an inline buffer; the imported scaffold's storage_path was a String

HISS-15 is mechanised per crate. crates/aegis-vulcan/tests/public_surface.rs and crates/aegis-hestia/tests/public_surface.rs require every public name a crate's src/ declares to appear as a whole identifier in some other integration test, and both collect public struct fields and pub static as well as functions, types, variants, trait items and constants. The floors are measured, not guessed: the scanner reports 155 names for aegis-vulcan and 143 for aegis-hestia, of which 25 and 26 respectively come from the field-and-static arm, so the floors are set at 150 and 138. Both figures are asserted rather than stated: each sweep runs the same walk twice, once with that arm and once without, and requires the difference to be exactly 25 or 26 and the keyword-only count -- 130 and 117 -- to be below the floor, so dropping the arm fails the gate

P03 and P15 stay proposals in planning/components.json; neither is activated. Neither crate is the component it is named after: aegis-vulcan maps no BAR and dispatches no DMA, and aegis-hestia runs no store and connects to no compositor, while those effects are what the two subsystems are. P15 additionally cannot be activated at this milestone even in principle: D09 makes it two halves, and verify_candidates() in tools/verify_preparation.py requires every candidate row of an activated component to record a manifest and a lock, which the Svelte half has neither of. The reference profile also records P03's peer-to-peer requirement as missing. The candidate rows keep manifest_present false because that flag is read by verify_candidates() as an activation claim rather than as a filesystem fact, and each row's note now says so and names the tracked workspace manifest and lock that do exist

Open decision D22 is settled by acting on it: the workspace member list is extended to cover both Rust candidates, which is the option the M01 register recommended, and REQ-WS-01's recorded defect -- that a workspace-wide cargo invocation would not reach them -- no longer holds. crates/aegis-vulcan/tests/manifest_hygiene.rs and crates/aegis-hestia/tests/manifest_hygiene.rs assert the membership, the absence of a glob, and the exact member count of five; crates/aegis-justitia/tests/manifest_hygiene.rs was amended from a single literal member line to the same name-by-name check, because five entries no longer fit on one line and a literal would assert formatting rather than content

Gates re-run on the reference profile, each exit 0: `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo build --locked`, `cargo test --locked --all-features` (542 cases over 67 test binaries and 5 doc-test groups, of which 182 cases over 27 binaries and 2 doc-test groups are the two new crates; 360 before this milestone), `cargo clippy --locked --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`, `RUSTDOCFLAGS='-D warnings' cargo doc --locked --no-deps`, `make verify-all`, `python3 tools/rank_roadmap.py`, `npx --yes markdownlint-cli2@0.23.2`, `yamllint .`, `flake8 .` and `black --check --line-length 100 tools .config/agent/hooks`

Scope: two validation libraries and three payload schemas, checked on the reference profile recorded in planning/hardware-profile.json. What was produced is arithmetic, bounds and encodings. No VFIO container is opened, no BAR is mapped, no DMA-BUF is exported or imported, no NVMe or GPU transfer is issued, no PGlite instance is started, no Btrfs subvolume is touched, no Wayland compositor is reached, and no transport carries any of the three payloads. The render-node readings are development evidence about one workstation and close no hardware gate: P03's peer-to-peer requirement is still recorded as missing there, and the native build, image, boot, hardware, accessibility and release gates all remain blocked

reference_profile.rationale: Moves up two places, 9 -> 7. Its only consumer used to be M12, the most deeply blocked milestone in the graph (needs Imago, Nucleus AND hardware this machine lacks). With the M12 split, M17 now feeds M25, which is locally executable on the reference profile. Its descendants stay 2 and its cost stays trivial, so score is unchanged at 3.0 — the movement is the availability change: its output stops being blocked behind a milestone that cannot run on this profile and starts feeding one that can.

exit_criteria: crates/aegis-tellus and crates/aegis-athena have manifests, lock entries and positive/negative/boundary tests passing under cargo test and clippy; the Rust toolchain from M02 is reused and no new toolchain is admitted

epics.title: Tellus SCI arithmetic
epics.acceptance: Positive: a hand-computed SCI matches. Negative: functional_units <= 0 falls back without NaN. Boundary: 300.0 is not deferred, 300.001 is deferred, and slices never exceed 16.

epics.title: Athena lifecycle and Pareto gate
epics.acceptance: Positive: a passing candidate reaches Publish. Negative: exceeding any single bound reaches Invalidate with a ledger entry, and an empty id is rejected. Boundary: latency 1.5 and retention 0.99 are exercised exactly.

epics.acceptance: Positive: a chain re-walk verifies. Negative: a tampered record is detected. Boundary: the genesis record is verified, and the algorithm matches D02.

evidence: crates/aegis-tellus and crates/aegis-athena are workspace members. The root Cargo.toml lists seven members written out one per line with no glob; Cargo.lock gains one [[package]] entry per crate and resolves no new third-party crate (aegis-tellus: serde, serde_json, thiserror; aegis-athena: those three plus the two workspace path dependencies aegis-justitia and aegis-tellus). `git status --porcelain Cargo.lock` shows the lock modified rather than regenerated, and `git diff Cargo.lock` is 20 added lines and no removed line. The toolchain admitted at M02 is reused unchanged: neither rust-toolchain.toml nor docs/roadmap/toolchain-admission.md is edited, and `rustup show active-toolchain` reports 1.98.1-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu overridden by rust-toolchain.toml. Both crates are libraries: no [[bin]], publish = false, and [lints] workspace = true so unsafe_code = "forbid" is inherited rather than restated

789 Rust tests pass across the workspace under `cargo test --locked --all-features`, of which 117 are aegis-tellus and 122 are aegis-athena. `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo build --locked`, `cargo clippy --locked --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings` and `RUSTDOCFLAGS='-D warnings' cargo doc --locked --no-deps` all exit 0, as do `make verify-all`, `python3 tools/rank_roadmap.py`, `python3 -B -m unittest discover -s tools -p 'test_*.py'`, `npx --yes markdownlint-cli2@0.23.2`, `yamllint .` and `flake8 .`. The clippy run was forced rather than cached: every `crates/*/src/**.rs` file was touched first and clippy re-checked all seven workspace members

E05-1, the SCI arithmetic. `SciEngine::sci_rate` (crates/aegis-tellus/src/sci.rs) is REQ-P13-01's ((E*I)+M)/R and nothing else. Positive: the scaffold's own benchmark inputs, energy 0.0025 kWh at the recorded default intensity 220.0 gCO2eq/kWh and embodied carbon 0.05 gCO2eq over one functional unit, hand-compute to 0.6 and the engine returns it within 1e-12. Negative: a functional-unit count of 0.0, -0.0, -1.0, NaN, an infinity, a subnormal or -f64::MAX falls back to 1.0 and the resulting rate is asserted non-NaN and finite, which is the half a fell_back flag alone does not cover. Boundary: the defer comparison is strict, so 300.0 does not defer, 300.001 does, and the next representable f64 above 300.0 does; the slice table is a fixed array of 16 and the seventeenth push is refused without changing the table

E05-1's finiteness claim is bound to a falsifier rather than asserted. Every input reaches the arithmetic through a validating constructor with a recorded bound, so the largest numerator the admitted domain can produce is 2.000001e9 and the smallest divisor 1e-6; `SciCalculation::as_rate` refuses anything outside 0.0..=MAX_SCI_RATE and crates/aegis-tellus/tests/sci_arithmetic.rs drives it at the extremes of all three bounded inputs and across the nine recorded hostile functional-unit counts. Widening a bound past the point where the division overflows fails that test

E05-2, the Athena lifecycle and Pareto gate. `Lifecycle` (crates/aegis-athena/src/machine.rs) is REQ-P16-01's seven stages, with only Invalidate terminal: Publish accepts a withdrawal, which is REQ-P16-05's reversible maturity gate rather than an oversight. Positive: a candidate at the scaffold's own sample metrics reaches Publish. Negative: breaching each of the four bounds in turn reaches Invalidate and writes exactly one ledger record, and the empty candidate identifier the scaffold guards with assert! does not become a value at all (HISS-07). Boundary: a latency of exactly 1.5 does not clear because the comparison is `< 1.5`, and a retention of exactly 0.99 does clear because that comparison is `>= 0.99`; the asymmetry is the scaffold's and is kept deliberately. REQ-P16-10's 500 ms check budget is enforced rather than reported: exactly 500 is accepted and 501 is refused with the stage unchanged

E05-3, the ledger ported under D02. `CheckpointLedger` (crates/aegis-athena/src/ledger.rs) is generic over `aegis_justitia::LedgerHasher`, the trait M02 created, so the workspace has one hashing boundary and one implementation rather than two. Positive: an eight-record chain re-walks to its head digest. Negative: a record restated with one field changed and its stored digest left alone is detected as LedgerError::DigestMismatch at its sequence number, a sequence gap and a broken link are detected, and a backwards timestamp is refused on append. Boundary: an empty chain verifies as the all-zero genesis link, the first record's previous link is that same value, and the domain tag aegis.athena.checkpoint.v1 differs from the P06 audit domain so a record of one kind cannot be replayed as the other. The three algorithms the sources name are recorded in `register::LEDGER_ALGORITHM`; the code admits SHA-256 only, and no blake3, md5, md-5 or blake2 entry is resolved in Cargo.lock

E05-4, the edge contracts. P16 to P13 is `CandidateSciQuery` and `CandidateSciResponse` (crates/aegis-tellus/src/contracts/sci_query.rs), placed with P13 because the response carries an SCI rate only that crate can bound and because the dependency must run one way; P13 to P07 is `TaskShiftDirective`; P16 to P02 is `PromotionTrigger` (crates/aegis-athena/src/contracts/promotion.rs). Each round-trips through its own encoder and decoder, and each refuses an unknown version tag, an unknown field, a missing field, a renamed field, an out-of-charset identifier, an out-of-range quantity, a wrong edge and a payload past the 4096-byte bound. The M14 audit record is consumed, not redefined: `AuditIntake` decodes through aegis_justitia::SignedAuditRecord, so M14's version, genesis, refusal-reason and unsigned rules apply unchanged, and the one rule this side adds is which recorded decision admits a promotion

E05-4's two boundary cases. The sysupdate call is stubbed: `StubSysupdate` records what it was asked to do and performs nothing, and crates/aegis-athena/tests/stubbed_effects.rs sweeps the library for twenty recorded identifiers across two lists -- seventeen that are a finding anywhere outside a comment, including the OpenOptions call and the SystemTime::now the imported scaffold actually makes, and three that are a finding only outside a string literal because the graph vocabulary records them as data; the two lengths are pinned by the_watched_lists_are_their_recorded_lengths. That is a check over an enumeration and not a proof that no effect is reachable: an identifier nobody wrote down is not checked. A second check that is not an enumeration is held beside it, in both crates: no line of code under src/ names `std::` at all, every use being core::, crate::, serde:: or a workspace crate. no_line_under_src_names_the_standard_library fails when a line does -- verified by planting std::net::UdpSocket::bind and a std::env::var read, each of which the named lists pass. That second check is over the text of src/ and is not a proof over the category either: the standard macro prelude writes to a file descriptor without naming std::, so println!, eprintln!, print!, eprint! and dbg! walk past both sweeps. `print_stdout`, `print_stderr` and `dbg_macro` are denied in [workspace.lints.clippy] for that reason, and a grep for those five macro names over crates/*/src and crates/*/tests returns nothing, so the lints changed no source file. Verified in both directions: with println! planted in crates/aegis-athena/src/pareto.rs and eprintln! planted in crates/aegis-tellus/src/sci.rs, all three sweep tests still pass and clippy exited 0 before the lints were added and 101 after, naming each macro. An empty candidate list is handled explicitly rather than answered: `CandidateSciQuery::validate` returns ContractError::EmptyCandidateList, because an empty rate list and 'no candidate exceeded its bound' are the same bytes to a consumer that does not check, and P16 promotes on that answer

The wattage seam. `WattageSource` (crates/aegis-tellus/src/power.rs) is the boundary between the recorded simulated draw and the measured RAPL delta M21 will substitute; the arithmetic in sci.rs never learns where a number came from, because a source hands back Watts and `EnergyKwh::from_draw` converts a draw held over an interval. The recorded constants are derived transparently from the imported scaffold's simulated per-slice draws: core 20.8 W is its four CPU draws summed, the modelled DRAM figure 5.6 W is its four DRAM draws, and package-0 26.4 W is the two together. Every sample carries a `Provenance`, a test asserts that nothing this milestone produces carries Measured, and every zone's recorded label is pinned in both directions rather than only against Measured

D60 applied, against a measurement rather than against the sentence. `ls -d /sys/class/powercap/*` on this host returns exactly intel-rapl, intel-rapl:0 and intel-rapl:0:0; `cat /sys/class/powercap/*/name` reads package-0 and core; there is no dram and no psys zone; `cat /sys/class/powercap/*/max_energy_range_uj` reads 65532610987 for both; and `ls -l /sys/class/powercap/*/energy_uj` shows mode 0400 root-only, the CVE-2020-8694 mitigation. The seam therefore takes a ZoneList, a source refuses a zone it does not carry with TellusError::ZoneAbsent instead of answering zero, and a `dram` sample is labelled Provenance::Modelled. Two rules decide the label, and the roadmap states both because one does not cover all four arms of SimulatedWattage::recorded. For a zone the profile exposes, the label is the weakest of the figure's ingredients rather than the strongest, so package-0, whose recorded constant folds the modelled DRAM figure into a simulated core constant, is labelled Provenance::Simulated: Simulated ranks below Modelled in the type's ordering, SliceTable::provenance takes the minimum for the same reason, and labelling that sample Modelled would claim more for it than its core half supports. For a zone the profile exposes no counter for, the label is Modelled by D60's definition of that variant whatever figure stands in, which is why psys is Modelled while carrying the same SIMULATED_PACKAGE0_WATTS constant that package-0 carries as Simulated -- the package domain being the only model of the platform domain the scaffold supplies. This is a bound sentence, not an assertion: power_seam.rs::the_recorded_provenance_of_every_zone_is_pinned holds all four arms of SimulatedWattage::recorded, and flipping any one of them in either direction fails it. Both figures are recorded in `register` so M21's rollover boundary has a committed number to test against

Component activation: P13 and P16 deliberately stay `proposal`, on the same judgement M03, M15 and M17 made. crates/aegis-tellus is the SCI rate engine half of REQ-P13-08's mapping and is not the Kepler eBPF telemetry daemon the component is: it compiles, loads and attaches no probe, reads no counter and opens no bus. crates/aegis-athena is the lifecycle, the gate and the chain, and is not the P16 evolution daemon: it runs no candidate, invokes no systemd-sysupdate and writes no file. planning/components.json records each crate as evidence against the component's activation blockers rather than as the component

Scope limit: this milestone is evidence about arithmetic, state machines, a hash chain and payload shapes. Nothing here measures energy, loads an eBPF program, executes a candidate, deploys an update or boots anything, and no native build, image, boot, hardware, accessibility or release gate is closed or claimed.

reference_profile.rationale: Nominally down one place, 7 -> 8, purely because M18 and M15 sort above it on score; its own score is unchanged at 2.5. Ordered ahead of M06 at the same score on the tiebreak that it feeds both of the two milestones the profile most improves: M19 (eBPF verifier loads, now confirmed executable) and M21 (RAPL, now confirmed live).

Both crates are libraries: no [[bin]], no [build-dependencies], publish = false, and [lints] workspace = true so unsafe_code = "forbid" is inherited rather than restated

E06-1 is satisfied in crates/aegis-minerva. Positive: AlpsRouter::register accepts an expert and AlpsRouter::route returns it, with every registered field reading back (tests/alps_router.rs). Negative: route returns None for a domain no active expert serves, for a dormant expert, and for one drawing more than the declared envelope. Boundary: the 32nd expert is accepted and the 33rd is MinervaError::ExpertTableFull { max: 32 }; the 128th trajectory step is accepted and the 129th is TrajectoryBufferFull { max: 128 } (tests/trajectory_replay.rs); and relabelling flips only negative rewards -- a step at exactly Reward::NEUTRAL keeps its reward and keeps relabelled_goal None, which is exact because Reward is fixed-point in thousandths rather than the scaffold's f32

E06-2 is satisfied in crates/aegis-vesta. Positive: 64 microVMs and 128 capsules are accepted, and the tables report count(), running() and permitted_memory_bytes() over them (tests/microvm_controller.rs, tests/capsule_registry.rs). E06-3 is satisfied: decision D06 is recorded in crates/aegis-vesta/src/decision.rs as D06_WASM_RUNTIME, Closed on WasmRuntimeChoice::RustNativeRuntime, citing export-037 ce490c88081f by export id and digest prefix, and public:docs/integration/stack.md by tracked path with no digest restated here -- that file's sha256 is recorded once, in planning/candidates.json, where verify_public_citation in tools/verify_preparation.py rehashes the file against it on every run -- naming dispute DSP-25 and keeping both rejected options -- an out-of-process adapter and a direct Go dependency -- representable in the register. The choice is enforced in the type system rather than only recorded: AdmittedRuntime has one variant, so tests/contract_capsule_request.rs shows that a payload naming wazero, go-wasm-runtime or out-of-process-adapter does not decode. No Go crate dependency and no runtime dependency of any kind is declared; tests/manifest_hygiene.rs reads the manifest and refuses wasmtime, wasmer, wasmi, extism, wazero, kvm-ioctls, firecracker, vsock, io-uring, tokio, libc, bindgen, cc and any [build-dependencies] section. Venus (REQ-P10-02) and AF_VSOCK pricing (REQ-P10-03) stay deferred hardware-backed requirements: P10_RECORDED_CLAIMS records both as ClaimStatus::DeferredHardwareRequirement settled by M21, and tests/decision_register.rs asserts that status and that milestone. The public: prefix is bound to the file it names rather than to itself: verify_crate_citations() in tools/verify_preparation.py hashes docs/integration/stack.md and compares the first 12 characters, and it sweeps every workspace member's src/ and the two roadmap documents for the same citation shape. It is a check over the citations written in that shape, not a proof that every claim in a crate is sourced. The check was written after a Rust test comparing the constant with a copy of itself let a superseded prefix through, and replanting that prefix makes tools/verify_preparation.py name the file and line

E06-4 is satisfied across both crates and the M14 crate. The P06 action proposal is consumed, not redefined: crates/aegis-minerva/src/chain.rs builds aegis_justitia::ActionProposal from a ProposalDraft, reading ActionProposal::EDGE and ActionProposal::DIRECTION from P06's own constants, and tests/chain_contracts.rs round-trips the result through P06's own decoder. Negative: an unsealed draft and one carrying an empty seal are both refused as aegis_justitia::ContractError::Unsigned, which is P06's refusal rather than one of ours. Boundary: a dispatch at the capsule bound is accepted and CapsuleSlot::new(129) is SlotOutOfRange { slot: 129, max: 128 }, so a request past the bound never becomes a value; the same bound holds on the wire, where a payload carrying "slot":129 decodes as Malformed

The P09 to P10 capsule request is typed in crates/aegis-vesta/src/contracts/capsule_request.rs, where the consumer owns it, in the shape M14 set when it typed the proposal P09 produces inside P06's crate. It carries a vmm field of type VmmIdentity because D58 requires every measurement to record which monitor produced it, and both monitors round-trip. It also carries aegis_justitia::SandboxAdmissionPath, the type M14 recorded for the unresolved decision D04, so both readings of that decision are admitted and neither is settled by implementation. Negative tests cover a payload naming another contract version, an unknown field under deny_unknown_fields, an unknown capability name, an unknown monitor, the rejected runtime, the other edge this crate carries, and a fifth entry in a capability list bounded at four

The P09/P14 verification direction is typed with negative tests, and decision D27 stays open. crates/aegis-minerva/src/contracts/graph.rs declares CadVerificationDirection with both readings representable -- the graph of record's P09-submits and the dataflow document's P14-submits -- and src/decision.rs records D27_CAD_VERIFICATION_DIRECTION as Unresolved, citing export-062 1ce919ed54bb and export-002 7e0c95f4ea05 and naming dispute DSP-05. CadVerificationRequest is a submission, so it carries the graph of record's reading and refuses the other with ContractError::WrongDirection; tests/contract_cad_verification.rs shows the opposite reading decoding and then being refused, which is what keeps the reading representable rather than unspellable. What this milestone did not do is settle D27: a request type is a producer's statement about its own message, and the P14 slice is M08

The constraint screen is not a solver, and the type says so. The scaffold's NeuroSymbolicSolver returns is_valid after looking for an exclamation mark and fills a proof hash with the byte 0x42; crates/aegis-minerva/src/screen.rs keeps the recorded rule and renames the outcome to what it is -- ScreenOutcome is RejectedByScreen or NotRejected, with no variant meaning valid and no proof field at all. A script the screen rejected cannot be submitted: CadVerificationRequest::validate returns RejectedScriptSubmitted. No Z3 foreign-function interface is admitted, and P09_RECORDED_CLAIMS records REQ-P09-08's solver as ClaimStatus::DeferredDependency

No GPU, D-Bus, Z3 FFI, KVM or Wasm engine is used, and that is a regression gate over a named enumeration rather than a proof. crates/aegis-minerva/tests/stubbed_effects.rs sweeps the crate's own src/ for 22 identifiers (std::fs, std::process, Command::, cuda, cust::, nvml, z3::, z3_sys, dbus, zbus, tokio, reqwest, libc, RawFd, Instant::, SystemTime, thread::spawn and the rest) and crates/aegis-vesta/tests/stubbed_effects.rs for 22 more (kvm_ioctls, /dev/kvm, vmm_api, jailer, wasmtime, wasmer, wazero, extism, io_uring, iou::, vsock:: and the rest); both fail if one appears outside a comment, and both prove the sweep reports a planted line. An identifier that is not on a list is not checked, and the evidence says so. The two monitor tags firecracker and qemu-microvm are deliberately outside the vesta list because D58 requires a payload to name its monitor, so they appear in library code as data; a test asserts both that they are excluded and that they are present

HISS-03 is stated as a falsifiable property rather than as an absolute. Every value on a decision path in both crates is Copy, which tests/allocation_bounds.rs enforces by requiring Copy of 20 types in aegis-minerva and 22 in aegis-vesta -- a Vec, String or Box at any depth stops the file compiling. Decoding is explicitly not claimed to be allocation-free: both files decode a payload spelled with a \u002D JSON escape, which serde_json unescapes into a heap scratch buffer, and assert only that it decodes to the same value and that the decoded value still owns no heap

evidence: crates/aegis-ludus and crates/aegis-hephaestus are workspace members. The root Cargo.toml lists eleven members written out one per line with no glob, Cargo.lock gains a [[package]] entry for each, and `git status --porcelain Cargo.lock` shows the lock modified rather than regenerated. No new third-party crate is resolved: both manifests declare serde, serde_json and thiserror from the workspace table, and the only additional dependencies are path dependencies on crates already in the tree (aegis-ludus on aegis-justitia; aegis-hephaestus on aegis-justitia and aegis-minerva). Both crates are libraries: no [[bin]], no [build-dependencies], publish = false, and [lints] workspace = true so unsafe_code = "forbid" is inherited rather than restated

HISS-07 is what this milestone does to both scaffolds. Every refusal in export-033 and export-029 is a Box<dyn Error> built from a string literal, so a caller can only match on prose; crates/aegis-ludus/src/error.rs and crates/aegis-hephaestus/src/error.rs replace them with typed variants that carry the bound that was hit, and every test asserts the bound rather than a sentence. No .unwrap(), .expect(), panic!, todo!, unreachable!, assert! or unsafe appears in either crate's src/: the workspace denies the first six through [workspace.lints.clippy] and verify_library_aborts() in tools/verify_preparation.py sweeps every workspace member's src/ for the assert family, which is the mechanism the doc comments cannot be. A doctest assertion inside a //! comment is a test and is left alone

E08-1 is satisfied in crates/aegis-ludus. Positive: LaunchCommandLine::parse accepts 64 arguments with and without the recorded token prefix, and the scaffold's own sample command line parses into three arguments and authenticates (tests/launch_validator.rs). Negative: the 65th argument is LudusError::TooManyLaunchArguments { max: 64, at_least: 65 }, and a line of 500 arguments reports the same at_least, because the counter stops one past the bound and the refusal never claims a total it did not count. Boundary: the empty argument list is handled explicitly -- three spellings of it all parse and all report AuthenticationOutcome::EmptyCommandLine -- and its authentication outcome is recorded as a value rather than as the absence of one. The outcome is a three-variant enum because the scaffold's `token_found || !args.is_empty()` calls a line carrying no token authenticated; AuthenticationOutcome::scaffold_verdict keeps the old rule beside is_authenticated, and the test that compares them enumerates all three outcomes and finds the disagreement on exactly one, NoLaunchToken

E08-2 is satisfied in crates/aegis-hephaestus. Positive: BrepEvaluator::mesh accepts the scaffold's 120,000 elements and returns a MeshPlan carrying the size range it was asked for (tests/geometry_bounds.rs). Negative: a request naming no STEP source is HephaestusError::StepSourceMissing -- which is where the scaffold's `!step_path.exists()` lands, because this crate reads no filesystem and says so rather than pretending to stat one. Boundary: 500,000 elements are accepted and 500,001 is MeshElementsOutOfRange { elements: 500001, max: 500000 }, and the iteration bound is held: a walk of 1,000 faces is Completed { iterations: 1000 } and 1,001, 10,000 and usize::MAX are all StoppedAtIterationBound { max: 1000 }. Both bounds can actually be crossed here, which they cannot in the scaffold: its evaluation loop has an empty body and its meshing check compares the constant 120_000 with its own limit. CAD and solver versions are recorded as unpinned in src/register.rs as UNPINNED_DEPENDENCIES, five rows -- two kernels and the three named solvers -- each with is_pinned() returning false and a reason; tests/recorded_claims.rs requires a row per admitted solver, so the register cannot fall behind the set SolverAdmission admits

E08-3 is satisfied across both crates. Positive: both descriptors round-trip -- TransactionReceipt through crates/aegis-ludus/tests/contract_transaction_receipt.rs and GeometryViewport through crates/aegis-hephaestus/tests/contract_viewport.rs -- with every field read back and the wire form asserted, including "signature":"stubbed-unsigned-no-tpm2-binding" and "sealed-to":[7,11]. Negative: a receipt without a signature field is rejected; the field is required and has no default, so the payload is ContractError::Malformed rather than decoded into an assumed signing state, and the refusal still carries its correlation identifier. A receipt claiming a hardware signature is refused too, because ReceiptSigning has one variant and no tag exists for the claim. Boundary: a viewport descriptor at the mesh bound is accepted -- 500,000 elements encode and decode -- and 500,001 does not, because the descriptor carries MeshElementCount and therefore P14's own bound rather than a second copy of the number

The P09-to-P14 edge is consumed, not redefined, and decision D27 is not settled by consuming it. crates/aegis-hephaestus/src/verification.rs decodes aegis_minerva::CadVerificationRequest through the producer's own decoder and propagates the producer's ContractError unchanged, so an unknown version, an unknown field, an over-long payload, the other reading of D27 and a script the producer's own screen rejected all come back as the producer's variants (tests/verification_intake.rs). VerificationIntake::DIRECTION is read from CadVerificationRequest::DIRECTION rather than restated. What the intake cannot do is reach a verdict: VerificationOutcome has one variant, AdmittedPendingSolver, and is_verified() is an exhaustive match returning false, because no solver foreign-function interface is admitted in either crate; REQ-P14-04 is recorded as ClaimStatus::DeferredDependency. A test asserts that aegis_minerva::D27_CAD_VERIFICATION_DIRECTION still reads Unresolved, so closing D27 elsewhere fails this gate rather than passing silently

The P14-to-P15 and P11-to-P02 schemas are typed in their producers' crates, which is where every schema in this workspace lives except one. aegis-vulcan types both descriptors P03 hands out, including the one P15 receives, whose crate already existed; aegis-hestia types the registration P15 hands to P04; aegis-minerva types the request P09 submits to P14. The exception is the P09-to-P10 capsule request, which aegis-vesta owns because its bounds and its monitor identity are P10's rather than P09's. Neither schema here is like that -- the element bound on the viewport is MAX_MESH_ELEMENTS, which is P14's -- so both stay with their producers. Each carries its edge as a single-variant EdgeId, so a payload naming another edge does not decode, and each records that its edge is drawn by one source only: dispute DSP-19 lists P11->P02 and P14->P15 among the eight edges the graph of record draws and neither architecture document names, against open decision D37, and EdgeId::sources() returns 1 for both

The reference profile has a TPM2 and no FIDO2 authenticator, and crates/aegis-ludus/src/probe.rs records the three commands that established it: `ls /sys/class/tpm/` printed tpm0, `cat /sys/class/tpm/tpm0/tpm_version_major` printed 2, and `lsusb | grep -iE 'yubi|fido|solo|token|nitro'` printed nothing and exited 1 against the 17 devices lsusb listed. The two credentials are therefore recorded apart: REQ-P11-04's TPM2 sealing is ClaimStatus::DeferredHardwareRequirement, because the chip is present and no key is bound to it, while the FIDO2 half is ClaimStatus::ProcurementDependency, because there is nothing here to bind to and no amount of work in this repository changes that. tests/decision_register.rs asserts both statuses together, since what would be lost is the difference between them rather than either one alone. This is a dated reading of one workstation, taken by hand: the crate executes no command, no test re-runs any of them, and a host with neither device passes every test in the crate

D12 is applied and D48 is not settled. crates/aegis-ludus/src/decision.rs records D12_STEAMWORKS_EXCLUSION as Closed on SteamworksDisposition::ExcludedFromImage, citing export-019 b0aa6e54ed57 and export-004 15831276a058 by export identifier and digest prefix, naming dispute DSP-26 and ADR-0002 by tracked path, and keeping both rejected options representable. tests/no_steamworks.rs sweeps the crate's src/ for twelve spellings a vendored SDK, its binding generator or its shared library would name and proves the sweep reports a planted line; tests/manifest_hygiene.rs refuses sixteen dependency names on a declaration line and any [build-dependencies] section, and pins the [dependencies] table closed at exactly four declarations, so a dependency renamed past both name lists -- sdk = { package = "steamworks", path = "../vendor" } -- fails it too. Both are checks over the spellings they list, not proofs over a category, and the record's own names -- SteamworksDisposition, D12_STEAMWORKS_EXCLUSION and the ADR filename -- are deliberately outside the watch list, with a test asserting both that they are excluded and that they appear in library code. The image half of ADR-0002 is not claimed: this repository builds no image. D48_PRESENCE_INTEGRATION is recorded as Unresolved with both readings representable, which is why no rich-presence payload is typed and why the fourth exit criterion was amended rather than reported as met

Every value on a decision path in both crates is Copy, which tests/allocation_bounds.rs enforces by requiring Copy of 13 types in aegis-ludus and 21 in aegis-hephaestus -- a Vec, String or Box at any depth stops the file compiling. The floors are measured, not guessed: the scanner reports 139 names for aegis-ludus and 125 for aegis-hephaestus, of which 32 and 17 respectively come from the field-and-static arm, so the floors are set at 134 and 120. Both figures are asserted rather than stated: each sweep runs the same walk twice, once with that arm and once without, and requires the difference to be exactly 32 or 17 and the keyword-only count -- 107 and 108 -- to be below the floor, so dropping the arm fails the gate. The sweep found two public items no test reached and neither was papered over: LudusError's identifier variant was removed, because nothing in that crate can produce one, and HephaestusError's was kept and given a triple, because StepPath::parse is public and a caller crossing both does need the conversion

No SDK, socket, compositor, TPM2 handle, CAD kernel, mesher, solver or cgroup is reached, and that is a regression gate over named enumerations rather than a proof. crates/aegis-ludus/tests/stubbed_effects.rs sweeps the crate's own src/ for 20 identifiers (std::fs, std::process, std::net, UnixStream, /dev/tpm, /dev/tpmrm, tss_esapi, ctap, hidapi, pipewire, wayland, dma_buf and the rest) and crates/aegis-hephaestus/tests/stubbed_effects.rs for 22 more (std::path, PathBuf, exists(), Command::, truck, opencascade, manifold3d, gmsh, z3::, z3_sys, cgroups_rs, sys/fs/cgroup and the rest); both fail if one appears outside a comment, and both prove the sweep reports a planted line, including the scaffold's own `!step_path.exists()`. An identifier that is not on a list is not checked, and the evidence says so. Five strings are deliberately outside the two lists because the register has to carry them as data -- the sysfs probe path and lsusb in aegis-ludus, the two solver tags and the slice name in aegis-hephaestus -- and a test in each crate asserts both that they are excluded and that they are present. The SDK sweep in aegis-ludus keeps three more outside its own list for the same reason: the disposition type, the decision constant and the ADR filename are the record of the exclusion

evidence: crates/aegis-compositor, crates/aegis-lictor and crates/aegis-calliope are workspace members. The root Cargo.toml lists twelve members written out one per line with no glob, Cargo.lock gains a [[package]] entry for each, and `git status --porcelain Cargo.lock` shows the lock modified rather than regenerated -- the diff is 31 added lines and no removed line, so no third-party resolution changed. No new third-party crate is resolved: all three manifests declare serde, serde_json and thiserror from the workspace table, and the only additional dependencies are path dependencies on crates already in the tree (aegis-lictor on aegis-calliope and aegis-tellus; aegis-compositor on aegis-calliope and aegis-lictor). The crate graph is acyclic by construction: P08 depends on no sibling, P07 on P08 and P13, P04 on P08 and P07. The Rust toolchain admitted at M02 is reused unchanged -- `rustup show active-toolchain` prints 1.98.1-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu overridden by rust-toolchain.toml -- and neither rust-toolchain.toml nor docs/roadmap/toolchain-admission.md is edited. All three are libraries: no [[bin]], no [build-dependencies], no [dev-dependencies] -- each crate's tests reach its siblings through the same path dependencies the library declares, so a second declaration would be redundant -- publish = false, and [lints] workspace = true so unsafe_code = "forbid" is inherited rather than restated

E07-1 is satisfied in crates/aegis-compositor. Positive: 256 surfaces are accepted and every field of a row reads back, and 64 Tier-1 clients are admitted (tests/surface_registry.rs, tests/mesh_tiers.rs). Negative: the 257th surface is CompositorError::SurfaceRegistryFull { max: 256 } and the 65th client is ClientTableFull { max: 64 } -- where the scaffold accepts the connection and drops it inside an `if` -- and a duplicate surface identifier and a focus switch to a surface the registry does not hold are both refused, the second without clearing the focus the session already had. Boundary: the pacing constant is pinned (tests/pacing_constant.rs). REQ-P04-08 records three figures that cannot all describe one loop -- the scaffold's 100 us sleep, its own 144 Hz comment on the line above, and the graph of record's `<1.5ms (Render/IPC)` node budget -- and PINNED_FRAME_PERIOD_US is the refresh-rate reading, 6944 us, because only two of the three are periods at all and the 100 us literal is a 10 kHz period, 69 wakeups per frame. The pin is a DeclaredPeriodUs whose Display renders "6944 us (declared by refresh-rate-comment, unmeasured)", and the budget-fits-in-period check is shown to be falsifiable rather than vacuous

E07-2 is satisfied and the dependency was **not** admitted. Decision D08 is recorded in crates/aegis-compositor/src/decision.rs as D08_COMPOSITOR_IMPLEMENTATION, Closed on CompositorImplementation::PureRust per ADR-0001, citing export-013 7f4c22813332 and export-027 f19640d7a7da by export id and digest prefix, naming dispute DSP-23 and keeping both rejected options -- the C wlroots binding and the higher-level framework -- representable in the register while AdmittedBackend has one variant, so nothing in the crate can spell the superseded mandate. Two upstream checks were run at activation on 2026-09-13 and are recorded as UpstreamCheck values: zenoh reports max_stable 1.10.1, released 2026-09-07, against the export-006 proposal of "1.0", and smithay reports 0.7.0, released 2025-06-24. Each check carries two commands rather than one, and each was re-run verbatim from the recorded string: a version command `curl -sS -H 'User-Agent: aegis-os-upstream-check (https://github.com/cordanaLLM/Aegis-OS)' https://crates.io/api/v1/crates/<name> | jq -r '.crate.max_stable_version, (.versions[] | select(.num == "<version>") | .created_at)'`, and a dependency command against /api/v1/crates/<name>/<version>/dependencies grouping normal-kind rows by .optional. Both halves are load-bearing and both were verified by falsification: crates.io answers the same request without the User-Agent header with HTTP 403 and a zero-byte body, and the /api/v1/crates/<name> endpoint carries no dependency row at all, so the single header-less command this milestone first recorded reproduced neither figure. tests/decision_register.rs now requires the header, a crates.io API URL, and a dependency command naming the version, and asserts that the old header-less string fails that check. Neither is admitted at M07 and neither proposed requirement is inherited, which tests/decision_register.rs asserts as booleans rather than prose. The reason is recorded: the acceptance is a **mocked** transport test, zenoh 1.10.1 declares 44 normal-kind direct dependencies of which 42 are required, tokio among them, and this gate would execute none of them; smithay 0.7.0 declares 44 normal-kind direct dependencies too, but that 44 is the total and not a required count like zenoh's 42 -- 19 are required and 25 optional, and drm, gbm, input and libseat are four of the optional ones, all four inside the default feature closure by way of backend_drm, backend_gbm, backend_libinput and backend_session_libseat, so a default build would pull a system-library boundary into a milestone whose exit criteria forbid GPU and wlroots work. MockedMesh is the mock and is documented as one: tests/mesh_tiers.rs shows a publication round-tripping to a subscriber on the same key, a subscriber refused with CompositorError::RetroactivityRefused (REQ-P04-03's immutable read), and KeyExpr::parse("") refused as IdError::Empty with every separator shape checked

E07-3 is satisfied in crates/aegis-lictor. Positive: bursts below each threshold classify per the source's own comparison chain, and the scaffold's two processes register and arbitrate (tests/tier_classifier.rs, tests/broker_arbitration.rs). Negative: a focus switch to a process the broker never registered returns FocusOutcome::UnknownPid and throttles nothing, where the scaffold sets its active identifier to whatever it is handed and then throttles every background agent on behalf of a row it does not hold. Boundary: **every threshold is strict, and all three edges are pinned in both directions** -- a running average of exactly 100000 ns is Interactive and not Critical, because scx_cake.bpf.c writes `<` and not `<=` (export-056 39af243568ad); the same for 2000000 and 8000000. The EWMA is the source's own integer recurrence, (old * 3 + new) / 4 with the first sample seeding rather than folding, and a test walks a value down through two tiers to show the recurrence rather than the endpoints

E07-4 is satisfied in crates/aegis-calliope. Positive: 32 plugin slots and 64 DMA-BUF descriptors are accepted (tests/plugin_lifecycle.rs, tests/dma_buf_table.rs). Negative: the 33rd slot is CalliopeError::PluginTableFull { max: 32 }, the 65th descriptor is BufferTableFull { max: 64 }, and REQ-P08-03's Quarantine-before-Activation is a refusal rather than a sentence: Recognition to Activation is IllegalStageTransition. The transition table is checked at **all 25 ordered pairs** of the five recorded stages rather than at the handful a reader might think of, and the probe lifecycle likewise at all 16. Boundary: stride arithmetic is checked at 0, where the stride is 0 rather than a refusal, and at u32::MAX/4 = 1073741823, whose packed stride is 4294967292; one pixel wider is StrideOverflow rather than the wrapped product the scaffold's unchecked `width * 4` would give. A recorded conflict is carried rather than reconciled: the scaffold writes fourcc 0x34325641 under a comment naming both NV12 and ARGB, and that code spells AV24, which is neither, so PixelFormat admits the two formats the comment names -- each with its own bytes per pixel and therefore its own stride -- and PixelFormat::from_fourcc(SCAFFOLD_FOURCC) is UnknownPixelFormat

E07-5 is satisfied across all three crates, and each payload is owned by one crate rather than redefined. The focus-switch report (P04 to P07, REQ-P04-07) is declared in crates/aegis-lictor/src/contracts/focus_switch.rs, where the consumer owns it, and crates/aegis-compositor/src/chain.rs builds it from P07's own FocusSwitchReport::EDGE; it carries the cgroup slice the shell protocol's report_focus_switch request takes (export-035 4c2146ffed32), and SliceName requires the .slice suffix, so a name the broker could not resolve does not decode. The real-time grant (P07 to P08, REQ-P08-05) is declared in crates/aegis-calliope/src/contracts/realtime_grant.rs and built by crates/aegis-lictor/src/chain.rs. The DMA-BUF stream descriptor (P08 to P04, REQ-P08-04) is the one exception to the consumer-owns-it convention and the exception is structural rather than stylistic: P04's crate already depends on P08's, so declaring it in the consumer would close a cycle Cargo refuses outright, and crates/aegis-compositor/src/chain.rs decodes it through P08's own decoder. The P13 to P07 directive (REQ-P13-03) is not redeclared at all: it was typed by its producer at M05, and crates/aegis-lictor/src/chain.rs consumes aegis_tellus::TaskShiftDirective through P13's own decoder. Negative: malformed descriptors are refused at each edge, and two cases show a consumer validating more strictly than a producer -- a directive P13 accepts naming `background-builds` is IdError::NotASlice here, and a stream name P08 accepts at 48 bytes does not fit P04's 32-byte label.
